h: Wizards, football and a Watford climb
p: Got siblings of very different ages? Climbing is one of those rare activities where a seven-year-old and a fourteen-year-old can share a session without anyone getting bored, because each wall has its own level of challenge. Let the younger one pick the first wall, then hand the older one the job of finding the hardest route in the place. If you're also planning the Harry Potter studio tour on the same trip, put the climb on a different day or first thing, because both deserve fresh legs and full attention.

Watford has one huge draw for families just up the road in Leavesden: Warner Bros. Studio Tour London – The Making of Harry Potter. It's where the films were made, and you can walk through sets like the Great Hall, Diagon Alley and the Hogwarts Express platform. Tickets need booking in advance, but it makes a magical pairing with a climbing session for young wizards.

Football fans may want to see Vicarage Road, home of Watford FC, close to the town centre. Whippendell Woods, next to Cassiobury Park, is a beautiful ancient woodland with walking trails, especially lovely in bluebell season. The Grand Union Canal runs through the area too, perfect for a towpath stroll. Watford Museum on the High Street tells the story of the town's history and is free to visit. For food and shopping, the atria Watford shopping centre has plenty of options under one roof. Watford Junction station has fast trains to London Euston, so the town is easy to reach for families coming from the capital.
